name: jobs_calibration

targets.source: Atlanta Fed Wage Growth Tracker, wage-growth-data.xlsx (data dated 2026-10-08, downloaded 2026-11-21). Averages over the development months 2025-01..2025-07 of 3-month moving averages: job-switcher median 4.143 (data_overall, 'Job Switcher'); all-worker p25 -0.800, median 4.229, p75 14.471 (data_chart2).
targets.construction: The tracker defines growth as 100*ln(w_t/w_{t-12}), so a target is g/100 with no log(1+g) step. The tracker publishes only the median for job switchers, so p25 and p75 are the switcher median plus the all-worker gaps (p25 - median = -5.029, p75 - median = 10.242). This assumes switchers have the same spread as all workers, which is a modeled choice. Hourly wages and national data, against posted annual salary vs prior annual wage in NYC: known mismatches.

_notes: Targets are g/100, where g is the tracker's 100*ln wage growth (see targets.construction). The first version of this note said log(1 + g/100), which is wrong for this tracker; the difference is under 0.01.
The tracker is national; NYC is not separately available. Record this as a known mismatch.
64 per side, natural sampling (no stratification), calibration donors only, seeds 1000-1019, disjoint from the pilot's 0-19.
9 settings x 4 cells x 7 months x 20 seeds = 5,040 market builds with DA only; expect tens of minutes.
Run on 2026-11-21, after the frozen comparison, as a sensitivity: the frozen primary keeps the pilot values (w_wage 2, seeker_noise 0.75). Logged under later_additions in jobs_manifest.json.
